name: ceramic
summary: Glazed pottery: a banded jar, a plate, a cup. Fired clay with a glass skin on it.
why: Roughness 0.30, the second smoothest thing in the library after water's 0.08 and below a
blade's 0.32. A glaze is glass: it is the only surface in a tavern that returns a hard
highlight, and getting it wrong in the rough direction turns a jar into a lump of chalk.
Metallic 0.0. Glaze is a dielectric with a strong specular, which is the same thing water
is and the same trap - reaching for metallic to get the shine gives a pot made of pewter.
Depth 0.05, nearly flat, and this is the argument that matters. MU's pot sheets are bands
of painted colour - blue, white, orange - and painted bands are not relief. Read as height
they would corrugate a jar that is smooth by definition, because the whole point of firing a
glaze is that it comes out even.
